The lifting theorem D.50 of R24 concerns `F/R_nil(F)`, of which `M` is not a quotient: prove what it gives for `φ₀` and what it does not. State and prove what this gives for LM8 A.12 on the tripod. Prove or refute Lead 26 (a), and with it compute the obstruction for `φ₀`: its class in `H₂(M, Ẑ)` modulo the three centralizer commutators, in the coordinates of R7; it decides whether `φ₀` lifts to `𝒫₁`. Do the same for every member of the two families of R28. LM6 A.56 (R28) excludes lifts to `F/F‴` that commute with `G_K`; it does not exclude lifts.

`GT̂₀` and `GT̂` have no non-trivial element of finite order with `λ = 1`, and every non-trivial element `τ` of finite order is an involution `(−1, f_τ)`: LM4 D.32, D.34 (R25, refereed); cite them. For `Δ` of R24: `Δ(τ) = δ((1, f_τ))` (`referee/REFEREE_B_LM4_D34.md`), and `Δ(τ) = 0` when `τ` is conjugate in `GT̂₀` to complex conjugation. Prove or refute: `δ((1, f)) = 0` for every `f` such that `(−1, f)` is an involution of `GT̂₀`; and the same for the involutions of `GT̂`. An involution with `Δ = 1` is not conjugate to complex conjugation in `GT̂₀`, and answers LM4 D.12 in the negative.

Determine the centralizer in `𝒫` of the class of complex conjugation, with its torsion and its multipliers (the tripod form of LM4 D.63–D.65, R22). Prove or refute: every involution of `𝒫` is conjugate in `𝒫` to the class of complex conjugation; the same in `GT̂₀` (LM4 D.12) and in `GT̂` (the question of Lochak and Schneps, R25). That every non-trivial element of finite order of `𝒫` has multiplier `−1` is LM4 D.34 (R25, refereed); cite it, and decide whether the involution of R22 at type (0,4) induces one on the tripod when a puncture is filled. For the conjugacy start from D.34: `f = h⁻¹α(h)` with `h ∈ F′`, and `ψ : x ↦ x, y ↦ hyh⁻¹` is an automorphism of every `F^(p)`, on which `α = ψcψ⁻¹` (`c` complex conjugation). Prove or refute: `ψ` is onto `F`; `ψ` sends `z` to a conjugate of `z`; and, for `α ∈ GT̂₀`, the conjugating element can be taken in `GT̂₀`. The lifting theorem D.50 of R24 lifts the peripheral automorphisms of `F/R_nil(F)` with their conjugators: prove what it gives here. Prove or refute Lead 23: decide whether the decomposition of E.58.2 commutes with conjugation by complex conjugation `c` and whether `σ₂c` is an involution; determine `H¹(⟨c⟩, ℋ)` for the multiplier-one subgroup `ℋ` of `GT̂₀`, its map to `F₂` through `Δ`, and the number of conjugacy classes of involutions of `GT̂₀`. With 3 and 4, state and prove what follows for §52.2: which finite subgroups of `𝒫` exist, up to conjugacy. Cote 145, scan 23: the inverse image of `{1, τ}` (`τ` complex conjugation) in his extension is `C₂ * C₂ * C₂` on `τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞`, with `l_0 = τ_∞τ_1`, `l_1 = τ_0τ_∞`, `l_∞ = τ_1τ_0`; scans 28 and 29 attach the three lifts to the three arcs of the real locus. This is LM4 D.34 (R25) for complex conjugation. Prove or refute the generation criterion: an involution `α` of `𝒫` is conjugate to complex conjugation exactly when its three section classes contain involutions `t_0, t_1, t_∞` whose products are generators of the three inertia groups and which generate `F ⋊_α C₂` (a surjection of the completed `C₂ * C₂ * C₂` onto it is then an isomorphism, because a surjective endomorphism of `F` is bijective). The case to decide is the glued involution of Lead 23: prove or refute that it exists, and that its three lifts generate. Prove or refute Lead 26 (b), and use it: for `U = F′F³` and for the kernel `U₁₂` of the map of `F` to `SL₂(Z/12)/±1` on which `Δ` is read (R24), determine the conjugacy classes of involutions of `Out^♯(F/R_nil(U))` over the class of `c` on `F/R_nil(F)`, with the value of `Δ` on each, and decide for each class whether it extends to a compatible family of involutions over every smaller `U`.

The ghost structure theorem (the ghost-symmetries translation, item GS4; ghosts as defined in its section 2.2). Prove or refute: for open normal V ⊂ U, the ghost value map from the U-ghosts to the conjugator triples in B̂/R_nil(V) is injective modulo V-ghosts, and its image is the set of triples LM7_PUSH E.58 allows; the U-ghosts modulo V-ghosts form an abelian group exactly when the centralizers at level V are abelian modulo ⟨s⟩, ⟨r⟩, ⟨τ⟩; the commutator of a p-component and a q-component of two elements of `GT̂₀` is a ghost, with its value computed.
Prove or refute Lead 8 and Lead 9, with the normalization under which `D(F) = F` is literally the pair of equations (30) of scan 240.

Open Nakamura–Tsunogai (and its sequels), Nakamura–Schneps and Lochak–Schneps, and prove or refute Lead 10 by an explicit substitution between the equation of §47, the harmonic and equianharmonic equations, and relation (III′). Prove or refute Lead 24, with the degree-two map between the pictures of level 3 and level 4 written out.
Prove or refute: `GT̂ ⊆ C^φ`.
Prove or refute: `C^φ = GT̂₀`.

For `ℓ ≥ 5`, determine the set `{(F^(ℓ), D(F)^(ℓ)) : F ∈ GT̂₀}` in the product of two copies of the pro-`ℓ` group of the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations: the diagonal, the whole product (R11 shows that every pair is induced by some relative action), or what lies between; and the same with `GT̂` in place of `GT̂₀`. By LM7_PUSH D.50 (R24, refereed) the first projection is onto the multiplier-one solutions whose pure map is an automorphism: use it. Prove or refute the corollary: `GT̂` is strictly contained in `GT̂₀`, because a lift by D.50 of a pro-`ℓ` solution with non-zero pentagon defect (R13) is not in `GT̂`.

Compute, in the characteristic envelope of level four (LM2 E.3: order 442368) and of every further level your method reaches, the residues of `GT̂₀` and of `GT̂` and those that satisfy (E.2.1) of LM2 in some gauge; with R14, prove what each computation decides about 3 and 4. Determine the smallest finite quotient of `GT̂₀` through which `Δ` factors, and give a program that evaluates `Δ` on every residue of that level.

Prove or refute Lead 11. That `(T, W)` is a homomorphism on the multiplier-one subgroup of `GT̂₀`, and that `Δ` is a continuous character of `GT̂₀` that vanishes on `G_Q`, is LM7_PUSH E.65 (R24, refereed, with its two gaps closed in `referee/REFEREE_B_E61_E65.md`); cite it. Determine the image of `(T, W)` on the multiplier-one subgroup of `GT̂₀` and on that of `C^φ`: it contains the pairs of the Galois image and the pair of the element of E.58. Prove or refute Lead 25: the covariance of LM7_PUSH E.61 at every level, the image of the two coordinates in the product of the two projective adelic norm-one groups, and the intersection of the maximal abelian extensions of `Q(i)` and of `Q(√−3)`. State what 3 and 4 give for LM7 D.19 (the coset of the CM coordinates that Galois misses), for the automorphism of LM7 D.46 (R14) and for LM2 C.d5. Prove or refute, with cote 145 (`archive_145_143/`): his pair `(γ, χ)` of scan 11 is the pair `(f, λ)` up to the gauge `g ↦ l_0^α g l_1^{−α}` (scan 7: `u(l_0) = l_0^p` and `uρ = int(g)ρu`, hence `u(l_1) = g l_1^p g⁻¹`, so `(p, g)` is `(λ, f⁻¹)` in his gauge and `g` is the cocycle, not a frame), and it is injective on his `Γ`, the commutant of `𝔖₃`, which is `GT̂₀`. The frames of E.65 are the conjugators by which an element moves the canonical splittings over the isotropy groups at `P` and at the harmonic points (scans 22 and 28); the frame of `r` is a primitive `A` of `g`, `g = A·ρ(A)⁻¹`. Determine `β` of scan 11 from the relation of scan 12, and prove or refute `β = ρ_F` of E.61. Prove or refute (the moonshine dictionary, item M1 (a)): for `F` of multiplier one the image of the pair of frames in `PSL₂(Z/12)` lies in the image of the centre `{1, 5, 7, 11}` of `SL₂(Z/12)`, and `Δ(F)` is its class modulo `±1` (Galois elements give 1 or 11, the element of E.58 gives 5, the lift of LM7 D.46 gives 7); give the formula for a general multiplier.

Prove or refute: `C^φ ⊆ ker Δ`. Then prove or refute: `C^φ = ker Δ`. The element of LM7_PUSH E.58 has `Δ = 1` (R24, refereed), so the first inclusion settles task 4 (`C^φ ≠ GT̂₀`); with task 3 it gives `Δ = 0` on `GT̂`, which is LM7_PUSH E.3, and then `GT̂ ⊆ ker Δ ⊊ GT̂₀`. Prove or refute `Δ = 0` on `GT̂` directly as well: from the pentagon in a quotient of the five-point group in which both coordinates are read; from the harmonic and equianharmonic equations and relation (III′) of task 2, deciding whether they hold for `F` exactly when `Δ(F) = 0`; and from the comparison characters of LM7_PUSH E.64 and E.67 (R24). A value `Δ = 1` on an element of `GT̂` gives a continuous quadratic character of `GT̂` that is trivial on `G_Q`, hence an element of `GT̂` outside the Galois image: write every step of such a proof out in full. Prove or refute also: the automorphism of LM7 D.46 (R14), with its conjugators, satisfies the hypotheses of E.58 for `U = ker(B̂ → SL₂(Z/12)/±1)`; if so, its lift is an element of `GT̂₀` of multiplier one with the CM pair of D.46 and `Δ = 1`, and LM7 D.19 for `GT̂₀` follows. The conjecture of cote 143, scans 29 to 31 (`archive_145_143/`), fails at type (0,3) in both written forms: arrow (1) an isomorphism, which there says `G_Q ≅ 𝒫`; and, with the commutation with `𝔖₃` that his two margins ask for, `G_Q ≅ GT̂₀`. Prove it from R24, or give the exact error. Prove or refute: an element of `GT̂₀` that preserves the conjugacy classes of the sections of the harmonic and of the equianharmonic point has `Δ = 0`; an element of `C^φ` preserves them. R29 (2): prove or refute ANABELIAN_149_PUSH E.14 with the cited theorems opened; state what the property AA imposes on an element of `GT̂` at the level of the tripod; and prove or refute: every closed subgroup of `GT̂` with the property AA lies in `ker Δ` (it holds for the conjugates of the Galois image, since `Δ` is invariant under conjugation and vanishes on `G_Q`).

Determine the group of continuous characters `GT̂₀ → F₂` that vanish on the Galois image, and the abelianization of the quotient of `GT̂₀` by the closed normal subgroup generated by the Galois image; prove or refute that `Δ` generates the first group. Determine in the same way the continuous characters of finite order of `GT̂` that vanish on the Galois image. Decide whether further characters of this kind arise at other levels: with `Z/2m`, `m = 12` and `m = 30`, in place of `Z/12`, and the frames at the corresponding levels, determine the characters of the multiplier-one subgroup of `GT̂₀` that vanish on the Galois image (the moonshine dictionary, item M1 (d)); Lead 25 says that at the harmonic and equianharmonic points `Δ` is the only one.

The resolvent maps (Lead 27 (a)). Define the maps `𝔗^{(5)}`, `𝔗^{(7)}`, `𝔗^{(11)}`, for every choice of the retained factors, on their domains. Prove that they are continuous homomorphisms preserving `λ`; determine for each the field over whose Galois group it is the identity; prove or refute `𝔗^{(p)}(F) = F` for every `F ∈ GT̂` in the domain, and state its relation to relations (III′) and (IV) of Nakamura–Schneps and to the equation of §47 (`C^φ` of task 3 is a fixed-point set of the same kind, for the quotient by `𝔖₃`). Compute each map on the element of LM7_PUSH E.58 and on the lift of LM7 D.46. Determine the common fixed subgroup of the whole family and compare it with `ker Δ`, with `C^φ`, and with the subgroups with the property AA of R29 (2); decide whether it is a condition of the kind that cote 143, scan 30, asks for (his "structure « locale » éventuelle").

The Lattès maps (Lead 27 (b)). Prove or refute: the statement on `L_α`, and its Gaussian analogue for quadrangulations; that the Galois group of `Q(ω)`, respectively of `Q(i)`, commutes with the family on dessins; that an element of `GT̂₀` commutes with the Eisenstein family exactly when `T` is the coordinate of a Galois element, and with the Gaussian family exactly when `W` is; and that commuting with both gives `Δ = 0`. Decide whether every element of `GT̂` commutes with both families.

`GT̂₀` on the congruence tower (the lambency translation, item L1). Prove or refute: every F ∈ `GT̂₀` preserves Γ̂(n) for every n and the conjugacy class of Γ̂₀(n); the induced automorphism of PSL₂(ℤ/n) is conjugation by an element of PGL₂(ℤ/n) of determinant λ(F); describe the induced map `GT̂₀` → PGL₂(Ẑ) and its kernel (the congruence ghosts).

Prove or refute Lead 12 and Lead 20; then compute `H^i_cts(G_Q, Z₅(j))` for `i = 0, 1, 2` and `j = 3, 4, 5`, each by `RΓ(Z[1/5], ·)` and an explicit residue complex, with Jannsen's sequence and its lim¹ term.

Compute the obstruction to lifting a class `(α, β)` of `Sec(T₂)` to `T₃`: two classes in `H²_cts(G_Q, Z₅(3))`, as explicit families of residues in the coordinates of R16. Prove the criterion for a lift (a tame condition at every prime together with a convergence condition) and determine every fibre of `Sec(T₃) → Sec(T₂)`.
Prove or refute Lead 13.
Determine `Sec(T₄)` and `Sec(T₅)` in the same form: the obstruction classes, the criterion, the fibres with the torsion of weight four, and the class-five obstruction of R17 at every prime.

Determine `Sec(F^(5)/(F^(5))″)`: by R15 it is the limit of the section sets of its nilpotent quotients; compute the cohomology of the Alexander module that this needs, give the limit, the images of the three unit cusp sections and of the tangential sections at the other tangent vectors, and decide whether it contains a class that is neither cuspidal nor the class of a rational point. R29 (3): for the Fermat curves of exponent `3^r` and `5^r` the full metabelian quotient has non-cuspidal section classes (LM6 E.33, E.34) while the full profinite group has none (LM6 E.12, given the local theorem). Prove these rows or give the exact error; decide the same for the tripod; decide whether the non-cuspidal classes of LM6 E.34 lift to `N/N^(m)` for every `m`, or determine the first `m` at which they stop, with the obstruction class; and prove or refute the hunch of the Fermat participant of the debate (Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max): no nilpotent quotient and no solvable quotient of fixed length has only cuspidal sections, and the quotient that is prosolvable over the cover with group `SL₂(F_ℓ)` of the Legendre family has only cuspidal ones.

For every 5-power level, determine the section set of the induced relative Fermat kernel of LM8 F.20–F.23 with unrestricted ramification, and prove or refute that it equals the section set of the metabelian completion of the Fermat covering of that level (the comparison that LM8 F.12 leaves out).
Prove or refute Lead 16; determine `Sec_{Q(μ_{5^∞})}(T_n)` for every `n`, and derive the answers to 2–4 again as descent data for `Γ`.

The smallest quotient that mixes two primes. Prove or refute Lead 18: for `Q₇₅` with the action of `G_Q` through the unit tangential base point at 0, determine the Galois module `F₂₅`, the map from `Sec(Q₇₅)` to the section set of the quotient of order three, its image (the obstruction class in `H²`) and every fibre as a torsor; and say, with proof, which of the two readings governs each of LM8 A.12, F.12 and G.20.

With `E_c` as in Lead 18: determine the classes of `H¹(G_Q, E_c[5])` that extend to a section of the relative pro-5 quotient `F/ker(K₃ → K₃^(5))` (through `E_c[5ⁿ]` for every `n` and through the quotient of LM8 A.23, with the local conditions that a section imposes at 3, at 5 and at the cusps), and prove or refute that they are exactly the Kummer classes of the rational points of `E_c` minus its three cusps and of the cusps. Then prove or refute the same statement for the classes that extend to a section of `F` itself.
Prove or refute (M0) and (M1) of Lead 19 for `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over `Q`, for `U` over `K`, and for every hyperbolic curve over a number field; tasks 8 and 9 are the first case of (M1).

For each of the twenty-four `(d, m, t)`: prove or refute `H¹_f(K, Q₅(ψ_d^{−m−t} ψ̄_d^{−t})) = 0` without modular symbols and without Kato's theorem: through Rubin's theorem for `K` at the split prime 5, the value at that character of the two-variable `p`-adic `L`-function (computed from Eisenstein–Kronecker numbers or elliptic units, to a precision proved to decide it), and the descent from the Iwasawa module to `H¹_f` with every hypothesis checked.

Recompute by your own program each of the twelve certificates modulo 25 of LM8 F.16–F.18 and confirm it or give the exact error. State the exact form of Kato's theorem that LM8 uses, prove that it applies to these CM forms, and prove or refute each step of the passage from the certificate to the vanishing (the control of the specialization, the restriction kernels, the lattice).
Prove or refute the vanishing for the balanced lines.

Where a vanishing fails, compute the true dimension, and recompute every entry of the tables of LM8 F.9 and the first strict levels (1 for `E₁`; 2, 3, 4 for `E₆` with 0, 1, 2 extra primes) that depend on it.

Prove or refute Lead 14. Determine exactly the germs `(S, Φ)` for which the category of coverings of the limit topos is `Rev(S, Φ)`: a characterization with proof, which decides the germ of `X` around a closed subset `Y` and the residual germ.

Prove: for a cofiltered system of coherent topoi with coherent transition morphisms the finite locally constant objects of the limit are the 2-colimit of those of the stages (derive it from SGA 4 VI, with the hypotheses). Apply it to the étale topoi of the punctured henselian neighbourhoods of a point of a smooth curve over a field of characteristic 0, and of a point of a normal crossings divisor with `r` branches: the limit, its fundamental group, and the comparison with LM8 E.10 over `C`, including the tangential fibre functors.

Write the parenthesis of scans 242–243 as a theorem in both readings: for which germs the limit topos is right, and by what it is replaced in the others. Open Leroy's thesis (R19) and say what it proves of this.
Prove or refute Lead 17 (a), and Lead 17 (b) with its torsor statement; compare (b) with CK C1, C2 (the packet as a torsor under the completed Kummer group).

Prove that "every section of the arithmetic fundamental group of `U` over `L` is a homotopy fixed point of `U` or of the homotopy limit of Lead 17 (b) at one of its cusps" is equivalent to the section conjecture for `U` in the form with cuspidal sections, with the exact hypotheses on `U` and `L` under which the two homotopy fixed point sets are the sets of points and of cuspidal sections.
Prove or refute each statement of Lead 21: (A), (B), (C) for a manifold and for an étale stack, and the three statements for schemes.
Determine `λ` of (G.25). Prove or refute Lead 15.
Determine the `Z₅`-lattice of the arithmetic image in the lattice of LM8 G.24: the values of `α` and `ν` on an element of the eighth Johnson subgroup of `Δ`, and the index.

Determine the embedded arithmetic image in every space of special derivations of degree 8 through 14 where a CM character occurs with multiplicity (LM8 G.14, G.15): each generator in the coordinates of the universal geometric space, with its `Z₅`-lattice.

Determine the images of the retained normalizer and conjugator data (`N_ρ^*`, `N_σ^*`, `G_D` and the two fibre products) on the integral `q₂` stage and on every higher relative stage of the Fermat tower.
Determine the kernels of these actions on every stage.
Prove or refute: every additive-polynomial lift of the first stage (LM8 B.24b) extends compatibly to every higher stage.
